events.title: The Holy League defeats the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto
events.description: Galleys of the Holy League under Don John of Austria destroyed most of the Ottoman fleet off western Greece. Lepanto was the last great battle of oared galleys and ended the image of Ottoman naval invincibility.
events.html: Galleys of the Holy League under Don John of Austria destroyed most of the Ottoman fleet off western Greece. Lepanto was the last great battle of oared galleys and ended the image of Ottoman naval invincibility.

events.title: A cyclone and storm surge devastate Calcutta and Bengal
events.description: A violent cyclone struck the Hooghly delta, wrecking ships and much of Calcutta. Contemporary reports put the dead at 300,000, a figure modern historians consider greatly exaggerated.
events.html: A violent cyclone struck the Hooghly delta, wrecking ships and much of Calcutta. Contemporary reports put the dead at 300,000, a figure modern historians consider greatly exaggerated.

events.title: Luna 3 photographs the far side of the Moon
events.description: The Soviet probe Luna 3 took the first photographs of the Moon's far side, which is never visible from Earth. The grainy images revealed a surface with far fewer dark lunar 'seas' than the near side.
events.html: The Soviet probe Luna 3 took the first photographs of the Moon's far side, which is never visible from Earth. The grainy images revealed a surface with far fewer dark lunar 'seas' than the near side.

events.title: The US and Britain begin air strikes on Afghanistan
events.description: American and British forces began bombing Taliban and al-Qaeda targets in Afghanistan, four weeks after the 11 September attacks. The war toppled the Taliban but lasted nearly twenty years.
events.html: American and British forces began bombing Taliban and al-Qaeda targets in Afghanistan, four weeks after the 11 September attacks. The war toppled the Taliban but lasted nearly twenty years.

events.title: The epoch of the Hebrew calendar
events.description: The Hebrew calendar counts its years from a date equivalent to 7 October 3761 BCE, the traditional date of creation calculated from biblical chronology. Year 1 of this reckoning is still used to number the Jewish year.
